payload.name: Preserve original date when enriching past-event memories
payload.description: During UPDATE or MERGE of an event/state memory, if new information on a different date is added, keep the original date/time explicitly in the content or create a separate memory; do not let the new date replace or obscure the old one.
content: When enriching an existing memory with new information that has a different date/time, preserve the original event's date/time explicitly in the updated memory content, and label which details belong to which time.
If a memory combines multiple events at different times, include each event's date or time in the content (e.g., 'On [date1], [fact1]; on [date2], [fact2]') instead of merging them under one date.

If the existing memory captures a durable fact (like an achievement) tied to a specific date, do not overwrite or blur that date when adding later related facts; either keep the date in the same memory or create a new memory for the later event.

solves: When a memory about a past event is later updated or enriched with a new event on a different date, the update can drop or obscure the original event's explicit date, partially erasing what was previously captured. This Skill applies when an UPDATE or MERGE operation would rewrite or append to an existing memory (event or state) that has a precise date or time context. The fix is to preserve the original temporal information, either by keeping it explicitly in the updated content or by splitting the new event into its own memory, so future questions about the original event remain answerable.
